svg.text: BEST FOR: WHERE THE MONEY GOES
FORMAT LINEAGE: Chip Huyen-style practical AI economics
Where the $0.68 per Agent Task Went — and the Four Levers That Took It to $0.06
A cost waterfall built from OpenTelemetry spans. Reference-harness decomposition of the measured before/after from IDEA-09; your split will differ, the levers will not.
COST PER COMPLETED TASK — BEFORE (LEFT), LEVERS (MIDDLE), AFTER (RIGHT)
Bars are USD per task; levers are applied in order, so each saving is measured after the previous one.
THE FOUR LEVERS (GOOGLE CLOUD ⇄ OPEN SOURCE)
System prompt, rules, and tool schemas are identical every
turn — serve them from cache instead of re-billing them.
Vertex context caching ⇄ vLLM / SGLang prefix cache
Send triage and extraction to a small model; reserve the
ADK model router ⇄ LiteLLM router (Gemma 3 / Llama)
Block the third identical call; hard step and dollar ceilings
85 schemas cost 35K tokens per turn; three cost 2.4K. Index
the rest and load on demand.
HOW TO BUILD YOUR OWN WATERFALL (30 MINUTES WITH OPENTELEMETRY SPANS)
Tag every span with task_id, model, input/output tokens, cached tokens, tool name, retry flag, and judge flag → sum by category in BigQuery or ClickHouse → plot the waterfall →
apply one lever per week and keep the chart updated.
Cost per completed task — not per token — is the only unit that survives a budget review.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
IDEA-09 reference harness • vendor pricing: Anthropic prompt caching (cache reads ≈10% of input price), Vertex AI context caching discounts
